evals.prompt: I'm building a Flutter app that must work fully without internet and feel instant, syncing with the backend when connectivity returns. How should I structure the data layer and repository so the UI never waits on the network?
evals.expected_output: Establishes the local database as the single source of truth and the network as a sync mechanism. Repository emits cached data immediately (reactive local stream) and triggers background sync when connected, so the UI never blocks on the network. Follows clean architecture: BLoC watches a Stream<Either<Failure, T>>, domain use case → repository interface, data RepositoryImpl coordinating LocalDataSource (primary) and RemoteDataSource (sync).

assertions.text: Response makes the local database the source of truth and treats the network as a sync mechanism
Response has the repository emit cached data first (reactive stream) and sync in the background so the UI never waits on the network
Response integrates the pattern with clean architecture (LocalDataSource as primary, RemoteDataSource for sync, repository coordinating both)

evals.prompt: For my offline-first Flutter app I need to pick a local database. My data is highly relational with joins and I need schema migrations and reactive queries. What should I use and why? What if instead I only needed a simple NoSQL store with full-text search?
evals.expected_output: For relational data with joins, migrations, and reactive queries recommends Drift (SQLite, reactive streams, type-safe SQL, migrations). For a simple NoSQL store with full-text search recommends Isar. Mentions ObjectBox for highest write throughput/object graphs and PowerSync for managed sync, and warns that Hive is in maintenance mode (avoid for new projects).

assertions.text: Response recommends Drift for the relational + joins + migrations + reactive queries case
Response recommends Isar for the simple NoSQL + full-text search case
Response warns Hive is in maintenance mode and should be avoided for new projects

evals.prompt: When a user edits a product in my Flutter app I want the change to appear instantly, even offline, and be pushed to the server later. How do I implement this optimistic update correctly?
evals.expected_output: Shows an optimistic update: write to the local DB first (upsert) so the reactive stream updates the UI instantly, then enqueue the mutation in a persisted sync queue for later remote sync, returning success immediately. The queued operation is processed when connectivity is restored. UI reflects local state without waiting for the server.

assertions.text: Response writes to the local DB first so the UI updates instantly, then enqueues the mutation for remote sync
Response uses a persisted sync queue processed when connectivity is restored, rather than blocking on the network

evals.prompt: Implement a sync queue for my offline-first Flutter app that persists pending mutations across app restarts, processes them when the connection is restored, and retries failed operations with exponential backoff.
evals.expected_output: Describes a SyncQueueService backed by the local DB (persisted SyncOperation entries survive restarts) with enqueue, processQueue (called on connectivity restored) and retryFailed with exponential backoff. Operations carry entity/type/data. Processing is triggered by the connectivity 'restored' event, and failed ops are retried with increasing delay.

assertions.text: Response persists the sync queue in the local DB so pending mutations survive app restarts
Response processes the queue when connectivity is restored and retries failed operations with exponential backoff

evals.prompt: In my offline-first Flutter app the same record can be edited on two devices while offline, so I get conflicts when they sync. What conflict resolution strategies exist and how do I choose one?
evals.expected_output: Presents conflict resolution strategies and when to use each: last-write-wins (timestamp) for simple/low-conflict data, server-wins for authoritative data (e.g. inventory), client-wins when user edits must always override (e.g. notes), field-level merge for partial updates on complex objects, and user-prompted for high-value data where loss is unacceptable. Recommends choosing a strategy per entity type.

assertions.text: Response describes multiple conflict resolution strategies (e.g. last-write-wins, server-wins, client-wins, field-level merge, user-prompted)
Response advises choosing a conflict resolution strategy per entity type based on the data's characteristics

evals.prompt: How should I detect connectivity in my Flutter offline-first app and trigger a sync when the network comes back? I've seen apps that think they're online just because Wi-Fi is connected but there's no actual internet.
evals.expected_output: Recommends a ConnectivityService built on connectivity_plus that listens to onConnectivityChanged, but stresses that connectivity_plus only reports the network interface — an actual reachability check (e.g. a lightweight request/ping to a known endpoint) is needed to confirm real internet. Sync (processQueue) is triggered on the connectivity 'restored' event once reachability is confirmed.

assertions.text: Response uses connectivity_plus (onConnectivityChanged) to detect connectivity changes
Response notes that connectivity_plus only reports the interface and an actual reachability/internet check is required to confirm real connectivity
Response triggers sync (processes the queue) when connectivity is restored
